root.name: Scandinavian Defense: Kiel Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. d4 Nxd5 4. c4 Nb4

overview: After 1.e4 d5 2.exd5 Nf6 3.d4 Nxd5 4.c4 White gains a tempo on the knight, and Black plays 4...Nb4 attacking c2 and d3. White usually defends with 5.Nf3 or 5.Nc3 and keeps the space, while Black threatens ...Nc2+ forking. The play is concrete and unbalanced.

white_ideas.idea: Use c4 and d4 space and develop quickly with Nf3 and Nc3
Neutralise the Nb4 with Bd3 or a3

typical_structures.structure: White broad pawn centre c4/d4 against a Black knight raid on the queenside

character.notes: Early knight raid and the Nc2+ fork threats give concrete tactics.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

soundness.notes: Probably better for White but not refuted.

structure.notes: Scandinavian structure with White's centre vs Black piece play, semi-open.

approach.notes: Rare sideline of a respectable opening.

sublines_that_differ.name: Marshall Variation
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 d5 2. exd5 Nf6 3. d4 Nxd5 4. c4 Nb6
sublines_that_differ.how: The usual retreat, solid and standard

character.reason: Knight raid and fork threats make play concrete.

gambit.reason: Pawns are even after the recapture on d5.

structure.reason: Scandinavian structure with a half-open d-file.

approach.reason: A sideline of the Scandinavian, which is respectable.

level.reason: Needs a few concrete tactics and ideas.

plans.reason: White space and development against a raiding knight.
